wins.text: Q1 revenue of $7.4B exceeded the high end of guidance, up 36% YoY; EPS of $0.96 up 55% YoY
Data Center segment revenue grew 57% YoY to $3.7B, driven by EPYC server CPU share gains and Instinct GPU ramp; operating income expanded to $932M (25% margin) vs. $541M (23%) a year ago
Client revenue grew 68% YoY to $2.3B with record client CPU ASPs; desktop channel sell-out up 50%+ YoY; Ryzen AI PC processor sales up 50%+ QoQ
Radeon 9070 Series launch set a first-week sell-out record, more than 10x higher than prior best Radeon launch, with strong ongoing demand
Returned $749M to shareholders via buybacks in Q1; $4B remaining in repurchase authorization

risks.text: New U.S. export license requirement for MI308X shipments to China creates a $700M revenue headwind in Q2 and an estimated $1.5B full-year 2025 revenue impact
Q2 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~43%, inclusive of ~$800M in inventory and related reserve charges tied to MI308 export controls
Data Center segment revenue expected to decline sequentially in Q2 due to MI308 China exclusion; GPU business will not grow YoY in Q2
Embedded segment revenue down 3% YoY and 11% QoQ; industrial inventory overhang persists with recovery expected only in H2 2025
Ongoing macro and trade policy uncertainty, including AI diffusion rules with a May 15 implementation date, creates longer-term TAM risk for AI accelerators

guidance_items.detail: Q2 revenue guided at ~$7.4B +/- $300M, representing 27% YoY growth despite $700M MI308 China headwind; full-year strong double-digit revenue growth reaffirmed
Q2 non-GAAP gross margin ~43%, inclusive of ~$800M inventory/reserve charge; excluding charge, gross margin ~54%; H2 gross margin expected to improve slightly above 54%
Client & Gaming segment revenue expected to increase double-digit percentage sequentially in Q2
Data Center segment revenue expected to decrease sequentially in Q2 due to MI308 China export control exclusion
Embedded segment revenue expected to be roughly flat sequentially in Q2; return to YoY growth expected in H2 2025
Full-year 2025 Data Center GPU expected to grow strong double digits YoY despite $1.5B China headwind; MI350 Series accelerated production on track for midyear

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Magnitude of Data Center GPU revenue in Q1 (analysts pressing for specific dollar figures management declined to provide explicitly)
Competitive positioning vs. customer-owned custom ASIC silicon and how hyperscalers apportion AI capex between GPUs and ASICs
Potential tariff-driven pull-ins in the Client segment inflating near-term demand
